name: M64 four-valve water-cooled cylinder head — creation preparation
description: Direction decided on October 12, 2026: a new four-valve water-cooled cylinder head, inspired by the 956/962 C Group C engines. The bionic fins remain an earlier, retained study. The private geometry derived from the 935 proxy is intact; the first proposed passages do not constitute a qualified sealed water jacket.

classification.intended_use: Documentary preparation, controlled CAD research and numerical verification only; no manufacturing or engine installation.

provenance.record_license: Repository licence for original records and code; third-party catalogue material is reference-only and private geometry is not redistributed.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics — 993 engine specification
sources.license: reference-only; no third-party images or text copied
sources.notes: Discovery and assembly context. Its proposed 4.0-litre build does not replace the project 3.6-litre historical baseline or establish our interfaces.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics — Swindon M64 24-valve head kit
sources.notes: Points to the manufacturer. Supplier fitment and performance claims are not transferred to this new head.

sources.title: Swindon Powertrain — M64 24-valve cylinder head kit
sources.notes: Published 40 mm intake and 33 mm exhaust valve diameters and 95–102.7 mm bore range are benchmark values only. Nominal 11.5:1–12:1 compression ratio is not a turbo design target.

sources.title: Porsche — 40 Years Group C, pages 18–19
sources.notes: Group C reference: water-cooled cylinder heads, independent circuits per bank and passages near the exhaust ports. No 962 dimension transferred. The cylinder-head/cylinder welding described by Porsche is not our manufacturing choice.

sources.title: Porsche — Turbo technology in motorsport
sources.notes: Distinguishes the initially air-cooled 962 IMSA from the 962 C, which also received a fully water-cooled 3.0 liter.

material.grade: not selected; hot-property and process qualification required

post_processing: Define datum machining, seat and guide bores, sealing faces and internal cleaning after geometry and alloy review.
supplier_requirements: Confirm access to the exact target donor and metrology scope.
Qualify the exact alloy, machine, process, orientation and heat treatment.
Provide traceable inspection, hot fatigue data and professional engineering review before any release.

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Head-body material remains unselected. Valve materials and their contacts are separate component decisions.

known_limits: Exact physical access to a 993 Turbo M64/60 head is unconfirmed.
The existing 935 scan is a proxy, not metrology of the exact target part.
Existing native CAD and rejected mesh experiments are retained unchanged; this record does not claim a new complete head.
Stud pattern, sealing register, hidden galleries and thermal loads are not established by catalogue images.
Four-valve packaging, twin ignition, actuation, lubrication and cooling require their own checks.
LLM benchmark scores do not qualify CAD, CFD, alloy, printing, fitment or engine operation.
The new water circuit is a routing assumption: heat to be removed, flow, pressure, radiator, pump, coolant and alloy remain unknown.
Oil lubrication is retained; air cooling of the cylinders remains the initial scope, to be revisited at the heat balance.
The decision to replace primary oil cooling comes from the owner's choice; no simulation here demonstrates that it is insufficient.
